attacks.claim: The embargo badge sets text to #ffffff on var(--surface), which is #ffffff in the default light theme. The label is invisible there, so the badge fails WCAG 1.4.3 and defeats its purpose. The color should use a theme token.
attacks.evidence: `.embargo { ... background: var(--surface); color: #ffffff; ... }` with `:root { --surface: #ffffff; ... }`; ABSENT: any contrast measurement or screenshot for either theme

attacks.claim: The unpublish control is a non-focusable span with only an onClick handler, no role, no tabIndex, no key handler, and no accessible name. Keyboard-only and screen-reader editors cannot operate it, which fails WCAG 2.1.1 and 4.1.2.
The description says the unpublish action appears 'on each queue row', but the diff renders it only when status is 'published'. The PR does not state which behavior is intended.
attacks.evidence: Description: "a one-click unpublish action on each queue row." Diff: `{draft.status === "published" && (<span className={styles.unpublish} onClick={handleUnpublish}>`

attacks.claim: handleUnpublish awaits onUnpublish with no try/catch and no error state. A failed or timed-out request is an unhandled rejection, the editor gets no feedback, and the story may still be live.
attacks.evidence: `if (ok) await onUnpublish(draft.id);` with ABSENT: try/catch or error feedback

attacks.claim: Unpublish is a state-changing action on live content, but the diff only gates it with a client-side status check. Server-side authorization for who may unpublish, and for which desk's stories, is not shown and must be verified before merge.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: server-side authz for unpublish. Client-only gate: `{draft.status === "published" && (<span ... onClick={handleUnpublish}>`

attacks.claim: The diff adds new branches (embargo badge visibility, unpublish gated by status, confirm-then-call) with no tests. Regressions in the destructive path, including the cancel path, would go unnoticed.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any test file for DraftRow covering embargo rendering, the published-only unpublish condition, or the confirm-gated onUnpublish call

attacks.claim: The unpublish trigger has no pending or disabled state. A slow request invites repeated clicks, each of which can open another confirm and issue another unpublish call.
attacks.evidence: `<span className={styles.unpublish} onClick={handleUnpublish}>` with `if (ok) await onUnpublish(draft.id);` and no loading state

attacks.claim: The row's status is not shown to refresh after unpublish in this diff, so it may keep displaying 'published' and invite a redundant retry.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: refetch or state update after `await onUnpublish(draft.id)` in the diff

attacks.claim: The destructive production action has no audit or telemetry event in the diff, so who unpublished what, and when, cannot be traced in this change. Server-side logging may exist but is not shown.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: logging, analytics, or audit call in handleUnpublish or the onUnpublish wiring

attacks.claim: The embargo time is shown with no timezone label, although the PR says it is in the newsroom timezone. Editors in other zones and screen-reader users hearing a bare time may misread the lift time. The formatInNewsroomTz implementation is not in the diff, so the conversion is unverified.
attacks.evidence: `Embargo until {formatInNewsroomTz(draft.embargoUntil!, "MMM d, HH:mm")}`; ABSENT: lib/time.ts implementation and tests

attacks.claim: Embargo state is computed from the client clock during render with no re-evaluation trigger. The badge can persist after the embargo lifts or be wrong under clock skew. The inline Date call also makes the branch hard to test without mocking the global clock.
attacks.evidence: `const embargoed = draft.embargoUntil !== null && new Date(draft.embargoUntil) > new Date();`

attacks.claim: A trash icon signals deletion, but unpublish returns the story to drafts. The icon points editors toward the wrong outcome, and the confirm text does not fix the signal on the row.
attacks.evidence: `<TrashIcon aria-hidden="true" />` in the row; confirm body: "will be removed from the site and returned to drafts."

attacks.claim: onUnpublish is added as a required prop, but the diff changes no parent or other DraftRow caller. Any other render site will fail to compile or lack the handler.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: changes to the queue list or other DraftRow callers; `type Props` adds required `onUnpublish: (id: string) => Promise<void>;`

attacks.claim: The confirm copy names 'returned to drafts' as the only rollback. The PR does not say whether re-publishing restores the original timestamp, URL, and syndication state, or whether feeds and external subscribers are recalled by unpublish.
attacks.evidence: body: `"${draft.headline}" will be removed from the site and returned to drafts.`
